findings.title: Specific instead of general sub-processor authorization
findings.deviation: Clause 4.1 requires specific written authorization for each sub-processor, whereas the standard preference is for a general written authorization model.
findings.impact: AtliQ must obtain individual approval for every new sub-processor or change in providers, which may delay operational scaling or infrastructure updates.
findings.quote: The Processor shall not engage another processor without the Controller's prior specific written authorisation.
findings.counterPosition: The Processor may engage sub-processors under a general written authorisation, provided that the Processor informs the Controller of any intended changes and gives the Controller the opportunity to object.

findings.title: No sub-processors currently authorized
findings.deviation: Clause 4.2 states no sub-processors are authorized at the date of the Annex, which likely conflicts with AtliQ's use of cloud providers or internal support systems.
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in immediate breach upon processing any data if existing third-party infrastructure or internal affiliates are used.
findings.quote: No sub-processors are authorised at the date of this Annex.
findings.counterPosition: List all required sub-processors (e.g., cloud hosting providers and internal AtliQ entities) in an appendix to be authorized upon signature.

fine.note: Instruction-based processing in Section 2 matches the standard.
Personnel confidentiality obligations in clause 3.1 are standard.
The 48-hour breach notification window is acceptable for a processor-to-controller obligation.
Audit rights in clause 7.2 are reasonably limited to once per year on notice.
Data deletion and certification requirements in clause 7.3 align with standard data protection requirements.
